header.label: projects
header.title: Autogear: An Automatic Derailleur That Learns When to Shift
header.lede: An entrepreneurship project that became R&D in embedded machine learning: a plug-and-play box that shifts a regular bike's gears by itself, without a torque sensor, with a model that imitates an experienced cyclist and runs on an Arduino.

decisions.title: No torque sensor, by design
decisions.caption: o: what the box measures (cadence, IMU, current gear); τ: the pedal torque, never measured. The learned policy sees a window of k past observations to make up for it.

decisions.title: Two stages for a 95 / 3 / 2 split
decisions.caption: p₁: probability of a shift (stage 1); p₂: probability that it is upward (stage 2). θ is calibrated, typically between 0.5 and 0.8; the safeguards then filter â.

decisions.title: A model that fits on the board
decisions.caption: Each tree f_k is at most 4 comparisons deep: the whole ensemble costs at most 400 comparisons per decision, far within the 100 ms budget.

decisions.title: Judged like an experiment, not a demo
decisions.caption: McNemar's test. n₀₁, n₁₀: test samples that only one of the two models gets right. Below p = 0.05, the difference between them is real.
